stem: Why is early diagnosis of retinoblastoma critical regarding the tumor's spread to the rest of the body?

options.text: It can spread via the optic nerve into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).
It spreads primarily through the lacrimal ducts into the sinuses.
It moves through the cornea into the external environment.
It remains localized within the lens and never leaves the globe.

explanation: Extension into the optic nerve allows the tumor to reach the CSF and eventually the brain or the rest of the body through the blood.
rationale: Consider the anatomical structure that connects the eye directly to the central nervous system.

optionExplanations.A: Extension into the optic nerve allows the tumor to reach the CSF and eventually the brain or the rest of the body through the blood.
optionExplanations.B: The lacrimal system is related to tear drainage and is not the primary pathway for this intraocular tumor's metastasis.
optionExplanations.C: Tumors spread internally through vascular or neural pathways rather than exiting through the anterior surface of the eye.
optionExplanations.D: Retinoblastoma is malignant and can spread beyond the eye if not treated early, making localization a false assumption.

source.hint: Consider the anatomical structure that connects the eye directly to the central nervous system.
